I've been doing this rotation for 15 years on this same ground. My father did it before me. The land is flat, the well pump works, and I know this soil. I don't overthink it — I follow what has worked and what my neighbors do.

I plant wheat every October on all 20 mu. I buy improved variety seed from the township supply co-op, the same kind I've used the last few years — it does well and the station recommends it. Before planting I plough the field, then apply compound fertilizer as base, and topdress urea in spring around jointing. I irrigate 3 times: once before sowing to get moisture right, once at jointing in April, once at heading. Two pesticide sprays — spring herbicide and a fungicide spray before harvest when stripe rust can show up. I expect around 475 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

After wheat harvest in June I go straight to maize on the same 20 mu. No time to waste — I rotary till lightly and seed hybrid maize the same week, usually Zhengdan 958 or whatever hybrid the co-op has in stock that year. Maize gets more nitrogen, I split it: base compound fertilizer plus a big urea topdress at the big bell stage. Summer rains help but I still irrigate twice — once if it's dry at establishment, once during grain fill in August. Two pesticide passes: herbicide early, then corn borer spray. I pull around 550 kg per mu most years.

My wife and eldest son do some work in town during slack periods, so I manage timing carefully — I don't take on anything I can't handle alone during peak planting and harvest.
